value.errors: unknown sku or customer_id raises KeyError
value.money: all money amounts are integer cents; no floats anywhere in the API

why: Defines the pricing API that invoice.py and tax.py will call: typed records, integer cents, discount rounding, and KeyError for unknown ids.

value.region: customer region code string such as "TX" (case-insensitive). None or a code not in rates.csv means 0% tax.
value.discount_pct: percent number, e.g. 10 for 10% off; None means 0. Applies to the taxable amount only.
value.lines: list of {"category": str, "amount": str}. amount is the line total (quantity x unit price) as a decimal string in currency units, e.g. "12.50". Pricing computes line totals. Category is matched case-insensitively after strip() against exempt_categories.csv; exempt categories are not taxed.
value.returns: dict {"tax_pct": str, "taxable_base": str, "tax": str}. tax_pct e.g. "8.25". taxable_base = taxable amount after discount, unrounded decimal string. tax = taxable_base * tax_pct / 100 rounded half-up to 0.01, decimal string e.g. "1.02".
value.money: no floats anywhere; all money is decimal strings in currency units, computed with Decimal
value.invoice_use: invoice.py calls compute_tax once per order with the customer region, discount and all line items, and displays tax_pct and tax. invoice.py must not apply tax rules.

why: Defines the tax.py interface so pricing and invoice know what to pass and what to expect. Tax rules come from data_tax/RULES.md.

value: integer cents everywhere (e.g. $12.50 -> 1250). Percents as integer hundredths of a percent (8.25% -> 825, 10% -> 1000, 0% -> 0).
why: Avoids float rounding; lets invoice do all rounding with integer math, half-up on the cent.

Accept. invoice.py will use get_item(sku).price_cents as list unit price and get_customer(id).discount_pct for the order-level discount (the spec shows list unit prices and discount on the subtotal, so I will NOT use price_for). Unknown sku/customer: I catch KeyError.

Accept. invoice passes region=Customer.region (None for unknown customer), discount_pct as int percent (0 if unknown), lines as {category, amount} for KNOWN skus only with amount as a decimal string converted from integer cents. Returned tax_pct/tax strings are converted back to cents/percent by invoice for display.
Withdrawn: v1 used decimal strings, which conflicts with integer cents in pricing_api and money_units. Re-proposing as v2.

Integer cents is fine, but percents as integer hundredths cannot represent rates.csv: NY is 8.875%, which is not an integer number of hundredths. Please use parts per million for the tax rate (8.25% -> 82500, 8.875% -> 88750). Tax rounding stays in tax.py because RULES.md defines it; invoice should not recompute tax.
Withdrawn by agent3: superseded by v2 (pricing_api uses integer percent discount_pct and tax_api uses decimal-string tax_pct). Re-proposing with the conversion rule at the invoice boundary.
v1 tax_inputs says invoice passes a taxable amount; agent2's tax design needs undiscounted line totals plus discount_pct. Withdrawing v1 to propose v2.

Accepting the functions and integer-cents rule. Clarification that supersedes the tax_inputs sentence: invoice passes Customer.region and Customer.discount_pct plus UNDISCOUNTED line totals (quantity x Item.price_cents, by category) to tax; pricing never computes tax and price_for is display-only.

agent2 reading: tax.compute_tax receives Customer.region, Customer.discount_pct (int 0-100), and UNDISCOUNTED line totals in integer cents (quantity x Item.price_cents) with each item's category. tax.py applies the discount itself. This overrides the tax_inputs sentence as agent1 clarified.
